description: "Working recipes for read-only prod evidence in WEVO (Aurora via customer-api pod, wevo-pulse DB with RLS bypass, log retention limits, Auth0 SAML user lookup) learned 2026-10-14"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 80a4365c-4ccf-4c24-a444-f084eefffdd2
  modified: 2026-10-14T17:39:59.388Z
---

- The old `remote-db-tunnel` SSH bastion (zuul.wevoconversion.com, key ~/.ssh/wevo) no longer works and the Duplo DBs have new hosts. Read-only SQL path that works: `kubectl --context prod -n duploservices-prod exec -i deploy/customer-api -c customer-api` and run node with `NODE_PATH=/wevo/app/node_modules` + `pg`, using the pod's `POSTGRES_*` env (user defaults to `wevo_admin`), with `SET default_transaction_read_only = on`. Helper scripts lived at `/tmp/wevo-inv/runq.sh` (Aurora) and `/tmp/wevo-inv/runpq.sh` (pulse_db).
- To replay customer-api service logic read-only inside the pod, an `.mjs` script must first `await config.initialize()` from `/wevo/app/src/config/service.js` (fetches SSM `/prod/customer-api/app/`) before importing models/services; the app has no `.env`.
- wevo-pulse prod DB: `duplopersonas-prod` / `pulse_db`, reachable from `deploy/personas-api` with `/app/.venv/bin/python` + psycopg2 and `DB_*` env. Tenant tables (`legacy_session`, `sow`, …) use RLS via `matches_tenant(owner_sub, org_id)`; for read-only reporting run `SET app.is_service_role = 'true'` first or every query returns zero rows. Native Pulse sessions live in `legacy_session` (`source_system='native'`), not `pulse`.
- Prod container logs are only what `kubectl logs` holds; there is no CloudWatch/Datadog log group for EKS apps, so a `kubectl rollout restart` (seen 2026-10-14 06:02 UTC from an IST operator) wipes history. customer-api logs decoded Auth0 claims per request (`user info extracted`), which is the only way to see a user's token claims.
- Accenture SAML users in Auth0 have `email: null`; search by `user_id` (`samlp|org-Nik2XGWIuvXhmqtQ-sso-connection|<email>`) or `identities.connection:"…"`. Org `org_Nik2XGWIuvXhmqtQ` = company 136, team 138; `pulse_user` role carries `access:pulse3.0`, so Accenture creates native Pulses in wevo-pulse since ~2026-09-24.

- Aurora users live in `wevo."user"` (singular, quoted; column `email_address`, citext), not `users`; team links in `wevo.team_to_user`. Pod env uses `POSTGRES_DATABASE` (`wevo_production`), not `POSTGRES_DB`. kubectl needs `/opt/homebrew/bin` on PATH for the `duploctl` credential plugin. The Auth0 M2M creds at SSM `/prod/shared/env/auth0_api_client_{domain,id,secret}` (profile `duplo.argus.wevo.ai`) work when the `auth0` CLI login has expired.

**How to apply:** use these before claiming production state; see [[wevo-prod-access-and-topology]] for profiles/contexts.

- AWS: profile `duplo.argus.wevo.ai` = prod account 900670598745; `duplo.argus-nonprod.wevo.ai` / `nonprod` = nonprod 380283542572 (ECR for both lives in 380283542572, region us-east-1). `default` = legacy account 844859623362.
- Kube contexts `prod` (duploinfra-prod) and `nonprod`; namespaces `duploservices-prod` / `duploservices-stage`. Pulse backend deployments are `personas-api`, `personas-api-beat`, `personas-api-worker-*`; env comes from k8s secrets `<app>-env-config` and `<app>-secrets`, which mirror SSM `/<tenant>/personas-api/env/{config,secrets}` (secret values are placeholder-created by Terraform and populated manually).
- Hostnames: prod Pulse API `https://personas-api.wevo.ai`, Pulse SPA `https://personas.wevo.ai`, customer-app `https://app.wevo.ai`; stage API `https://personas-api-stage.argus-nonprod.wevo.ai`, customer-app `https://staging-app.wevo.ai`. `prod.sandbox.wevo.ai` in customer-app `.env.production` is stale (TLS cert does not cover it); the real prod build reads SSM `/prod/customer-app/env/config`.
- Deploys: wevo-pulse "Deploy to Prod" workflow (workflow_dispatch from main with `release_tag`; migrations run from the release image before rollout); customer-app "Deploy to Prod" (dispatch from `staging` with a release tag). There is no `master`/`production` branch in use for customer-app; prod is a staging tag.
- Local targeted Terraform against nonprod tenant roots works with `DUPLO_HOST=https://duplo.argus-nonprod.wevo.ai DUPLO_TENANT=<dev|stage> AWS_PROFILE=duplo.argus-nonprod.wevo.ai` and `DUPLO_TOKEN` read from `~/.duplo/cache/duplo.argus-nonprod.wevo.ai,admin,duplo-creds.json` (check its `Expiration`; refresh with `duploctl --interactive`). Git-sourced modules need GitHub SSH (works). `-target` pulls in dependencies, so plan from a branch that includes current main or you will see reverts of newer applied changes. The `auth0` CLI's `wevo-staging` tenant login is broken (refresh_token grant not allowed); `wevo-dev` works via `--tenant wevo-dev.us.auth0.com`.
- `auth0` CLI is logged in with tenant `wevo-prod.us.auth0.com` active; `auth0 roles list --json`, `auth0 roles permissions list <id> --json`, `auth0 api get roles/<id>/users` work read-only.

**How to apply:** use these for read-only production evidence before claiming anything is deployed or configured. See [[figma-oauth-prod-rollout-2026-10]].

def _is_owner_scope_conflict(exc: IntegrityError) -> bool:
        diag = getattr(getattr(exc, "orig", None), "diag", None)
        return getattr(diag, "constraint_name", None) == THREAD_OWNER_SCOPE_CONSTRAINT

    @staticmethod
    def _load_or_create_thread(
        *,
        link: str,
        projection: PublicPulseShareResponse,
        findings_run_id: uuid.UUID | None,
    ) -> _PublicPulseChatThreadSnapshot:
        with get_service_session("public_pulse_chat") as session:
            row = PublicPulseChatService._require_chat_row(
                session=session,
                link=link,
                lock=True,
            )
            source_kind, scope_key, active_findings_run_id = PublicPulseChatService._thread_scope(
                row=row,
                projection=projection,
                findings_run_id=findings_run_id,
            )
            report_title, raw_context, compiled_context = (
                PublicPulseChatService._projection_context(projection)
            )
            conversation_owner_sub = PublicPulseChatService._conversation_owner_sub(row)
            thread = session.exec(
                select(PulseReportChatThread).where(
                    col(PulseReportChatThread.owner_sub) == conversation_owner_sub,
                    col(PulseReportChatThread.org_id) == row.org_id,
                    col(PulseReportChatThread.source_scope_key) == scope_key,
                )
            ).first()
            if thread is None:
                thread = PulseReportChatThread(
                    owner_sub=conversation_owner_sub,
                    org_id=row.org_id,
                    created_by_sub=conversation_owner_sub,
                    source_kind=source_kind,
                    source_scope_key=scope_key,

"""GrowthOS completion links must open for every project member (WEV-4154).

GrowthOS stores ``pulseLink`` once, at completion. The resume URL opens only for
the Pulse owner, so a completion that commits before anyone opens the share
dialog must still carry a public share link.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from datetime import UTC, datetime
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any

import pytest
from sqlalchemy import ARRAY, JSON, Column, MetaData, Table, Text, event
from sqlalchemy.dialects.postgresql import JSONB
from sqlalchemy.exc import CompileError
from sqlalchemy.pool import StaticPool
from sqlmodel import Session, SQLModel, col, create_engine, select

from app.models.auth0_directory import Auth0UserDirectory
from app.models.legacy_session import LegacySession, LegacySessionState, LegacySessionType
from app.models.org_webhook import OrgWebhookEvent, WebhookEventType
from app.models.pulse_share_link import PulseShareLink
from app.services import growthos_pulse_webhooks as growthos_webhooks

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from collections.abc import Iterator

    from sqlalchemy.engine import Engine


OWNER_SUB = "samlp|org-acn-sso-connection|owner@acn.example"


def _sqlite_column_type(column: Column[Any], engine: Engine) -> Any:
    if isinstance(column.type, ARRAY | JSONB):
        return JSON()
    try:
        column.type.compile(dialect=engine.dialect)
    except CompileError:
        return Text()
    return column.type


@pytest.fixture
def db(monkeypatch) -> Iterator[Session]:
    monkeypatch.setattr(growthos_webhooks.settings, "ENVIRONMENT", "test")
    monkeypatch.setattr(growthos_webhooks.settings, "GROWTHOS_WEBHOOK_PAYLOAD_MODE", "expanded")
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        growthos_webhooks.settings, "GROWTHOS_PULSE_RESUME_BASE_URL", "https://app.wevo.test"
    )
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        growthos_webhooks.settings,
        "GROWTHOS_PARTNER_API_BASE_URL",
        "https://receiver.example.com/wevo/pulse",
    )
    monkeypatch.setattr(growthos_webhooks.settings, "GROWTHOS_PARTNER_API_KEY", "super-secret")
    engine = create_engine(
        "sqlite://", connect_args={"check_same_thread": False}, poolclass=StaticPool
    )
    metadata = MetaData()
    for name in (
        "legacy_session",
        "pulse_public_share_link",
        "org_webhook_event",
        "auth0_user_directory",
    ):
        table = SQLModel.metadata.tables[name]
        Table(
            table.name,
            metadata,
            *[
                Column(c.name, _sqlite_column_type(c, engine), primary_key=c.primary_key)
                for c in table.columns
            ],
        )
    metadata.create_all(engine)
    with Session(engine) as session:
        session.add(Auth0UserDirectory(auth0_user_id=OWNER_SUB, email="owner@acn.example"))
        session.commit()
        # Only this session captures; the production listener is registered app-wide.
        event.listen(session, "before_flush", growthos_webhooks._capture_transition_events)
        yield session
    engine.dispose()


def _generating_compare(db: Session) -> LegacySession:
    pulse = LegacySession(
        org_id="org_acn",
        owner_sub=OWNER_SUB,
        created_by_sub=OWNER_SUB,
        session_type=LegacySessionType.COMPARE.value,
        display_name_override="Checkout vs Signup",
        growthos_project_id="c13b6163-project",
        state=LegacySessionState.FINDINGS_GENERATING.value,
    )
    db.add(pulse)
    db.commit()
    return pulse


def _complete(db: Session, pulse: LegacySession) -> dict[str, Any]:
    pulse.state = LegacySessionState.FINDINGS_READY.value
    db.add(pulse)
    db.commit()
    completion = db.exec(
        select(OrgWebhookEvent).where(
            col(OrgWebhookEvent.event_type) == WebhookEventType.PULSE_FINDINGS_COMPLETED
        )
    ).one()

`GROWTHOS_WEBHOOK_PAYLOAD_MODE=auto` is an explicit transition mode. It first sends the full payload, then on HTTP 400 for `pulse.findings_completed` immediately retries with the six-field legacy completion body below. That event retains its legacy projection for later retries, while every new event starts with the full payload again. The other five events have no legacy equivalent. Their HTTP 400 responses remain failed attempts and follow the bounded retry policy; they must never be converted into a completion or a billing transaction.

`expanded` sends full payloads without fallback. Both `auto` and `expanded` require `GROWTHOS_WEBHOOK_EXPANDED_PRODUCTION_APPROVED=true` for a production runtime or the production partner hostname because both can emit the expanded schema. That flag defaults false. The application default is `legacy`. Environment-specific desired configuration and actual deployment are separate facts; do not infer either from this default. Exercise `auto` or `expanded` only with a controlled receiver or a compatible staging endpoint.

The legacy completion projection has exactly six keys:

```json
{
  "userId": "owner@example.com",
  "projectId": "growthos-project-123",
  "name": "Checkout flow",
  "pulseLink": "https://beta.wevo.ai/pulse/sessions/share-link-123?hideHeader=true&hideAssistant=true&hideSidebar=true",
  "cost": 1,
  "reportType": "pulse"
}
```

## Links and the existing Discover action

`resumeUrl` is an authenticated deep link, preserving GrowthOS presentation and the two separate identifiers. It does not grant access to the Pulse. `pulseLink`/`findingsShareUrl` refer only to an existing active public share and include the GrowthOS presentation. They may be null if a share has not yet been created. Completion does not create a public share implicitly or bypass its authorization.

Customer App's existing **Send to Discover** dialog creates/copies a public report link for the user to paste into Discover. Clicking it is not an automatic webhook delivery acknowledgement. The automatic completion event can precede that dialog and therefore carry a null public link. The partner's null-link policy and any later link update must be agreed before claiming that the entire receiving workflow is ready.

The created share includes the owner's Assistant chat (WEV-4197). They are null only when the owner disabled public sharing, and `pulseLink` then falls back to `resumeUrl`.

-Customer App's existing **Send to Discover** dialog creates/copies a public report link for the user to paste into Discover. Clicking it is not an automatic webhook delivery acknowledgement. The automatic completion event can precede that dialog and therefore carry a null public link. The partner's null-link policy and any later link update must be agreed before claiming that the entire receiving workflow is ready.

+The link carries no `hideAssistant` parameter: the share's own `shareAssistantChat` setting decides whether the Assistant shows, so a later change still reaches the link GrowthOS stored. Customer App's **Send to Discover** dialog copies the same public link. Under the GrowthOS theme it turns on Assistant chat for the share and shows no toggle; elsewhere the **Include Assistant chat** toggle is unchanged. Clicking it is not an automatic webhook delivery acknowledgement.

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## Development Commands

```bash
# Development - Vite runs locally; backends run separately
yarn dev              # Start dev server (port 3030)
yarn start            # Alias for dev

# Code Quality
yarn lint             # ESLint check
yarn lint:fix         # ESLint auto-fix
yarn typecheck        # TypeScript check
yarn format           # Prettier format
yarn format:check     # Prettier check
yarn code-quality     # Run all checks (lint + typecheck + format:check)
yarn code-quality:fix # Fix lint and format issues
yarn code-quality:react # Run React Doctor on changed React code
yarn cleanup:react    # Fix lint/format issues, then run React Doctor

# Build
yarn build            # Production build
yarn build:staging    # Staging build
yarn build:production # Explicit production-mode build
yarn test:unit        # Vitest tests under src
```

Use Node 18.19.0 from `.nvmrc`, `nvm use`, and `corepack enable` for Yarn 4.1.1. CI uses Node 20.11.1. Use `yarn` for package operations. Formatting scripts cover `src` only. See [development and deployment](docs/development.md) for environment setup and the GitHub Actions release path.

Run `yarn code-quality:react` after substantive React/UI edits, before handing off large component or page changes, and when refactoring hard-coded styles or conditional rendering. Use `yarn cleanup:react` when you want the standard auto-fixes first and then a React Doctor pass.

## Architecture Overview

### Tech Stack

- **React 18** with Vite build system
- **TypeScript** for new code (Pulse feature), **JavaScript** for legacy code
- **Three UI systems**: MUI (legacy), Shadcn/UI (modern), Pulse custom components
- **State**: Redux + Redux Observable for global state, React Query for server state
- **Styling**: Tailwind CSS + MUI themes + Emotion
- **Routing**: React Router DOM v5
- **Auth**: Auth0

### Directory Structure

```
src/
├── components/          # Feature-organized components
│   ├── ui/              # Shadcn/UI components (TSX)
│   ├── pulse/           # Pulse feature - modern TSX + Tailwind
│   ├── dashboard/       # Dashboard feature (JSX + MUI)
│   ├── reports/         # Reports feature (JSX + MUI)
│   ├── intake/          # Intake flow (JSX + MUI)
│   ├── automated-insights/
│   └── auth/
├── modules/             # Redux modules (actions, reducers, epics)
│   ├── user/
│   ├── wevos/
│   ├── error/
│   └── notification/
├── hooks/               # Custom React hooks (useWevo, useTags, etc.)
├── routes/              # Route path definitions
├── api.js               # Axios instance with Auth0 token handling
├── theme.js             # MUI light theme
├── darkTheme.js         # MUI dark theme
├── globals.css          # Shadcn/UI CSS variables
└── store.js             # Redux store configuration
```

### Component Systems

**For new features**: Use Pulse components (`src/components/pulse/`) or Shadcn/UI (`src/components/ui/`) with Tailwind CSS and TypeScript.

**For existing features**: Maintain consistency with MUI components and JavaScript.

### Path Alias

Use `@/` to import from `src/`:

```tsx
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/button';
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils';
```

### API Layer

- Legacy Axios client in `src/api.js`, configured by `REACT_APP_CUSTOMER_API_HOST`, with Customer API token injection.
- Native Pulse client in `src/lib/wevoPulseClient.ts`, using vendored `@wevo/pulse-api-client` 15.0.0 and a separate Pulse token audience.
- Agreement operations use the access-service client and wevo-access token audience.
- React Query hooks manage server state. See [Pulse flows](docs/pulse-flows.md) and the [permission map](docs/permissions.md) before changing transport or capability checks.

### Pulse Launch Page

Before editing `PulseLaunchPage.tsx` or `AssetInputList.tsx`, read [PULSE_LAUNCH_PAGE.md](src/components/pulse/pages/PULSE_LAUNCH_PAGE.md). It documents the input glow bleed layout, scroll-container rules, and compare-card height constraints — easy to break if changed casually.

Before changing Pulse UI, footers, navigation, or button styling, read [docs/AGENT_EDIT_SCOPE.md](docs/AGENT_EDIT_SCOPE.md). Only modify what the user explicitly requested — do not restyle adjacent pages or swap launch vs session-step button patterns.

## Agent skills

### Issue tracker

Issues and PRDs are tracked in GitHub Issues. See `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`.

### Triage labels

Triage uses the canonical `needs-triage`, `needs-info`, `ready-for-agent`, `ready-for-human`, and `wontfix` labels. See `docs/agents/triage-labels.md`.

### Domain docs

This is a single-context repository with domain guidance in `CONTEXT.md` and architectural decisions in `docs/adr/`. See `docs/agents/domain.md`.

## Coding Conventions

### Colors

Always use hex codes for colors (e.g., `#276EB0`), never named colors.

### File Extensions

- `.tsx` for new TypeScript React components
- `.jsx` for legacy JavaScript React components (required by Vite)

### Styling Approach

- **Tailwind**: Use `cn()` utility from `@/lib/utils` for class composition
- **MUI**: Use `sx` prop or `styled()` for component styling
- **Pulse animations**: Import from `src/components/pulse/styles/animations.css`

### Key Colors

- MUI Primary: `#276EB0`
- Pulse Primary: `#3eb796`
- Light background: `#F3F8Fb`
- Dark background: `#192F41`

# sol-loop

This is a workflow for making your code changes more correct before (or
sometimes after) filing a pull request. tl;dr - use OpenAI's GPT Sol to review
your code in a loop.

Make the most minimal possible changes to appease the Sol reviewers. Be careful
of scope creep and don't be scared to push back.

## Budget

- Default: 3 rounds total. Round 1 is full. Later rounds check only
  changed code and open findings.
- Extend to 5 only for security, permissions, auth, data loss, or
  state/concurrency, while a blocker or should stays open with evidence. Or when
  the user asks.
- Stop early if a round returns only nits. Declined nits and comment,
  doc, or format-only fixes need no new round.
- One reviewer only. Sol must not start subagents or reviewers.
- Keep a ledger: id, severity, outcome, usage if returned. Never guess it.

## 1. Scope

Run `git status --short`. Do not stash, discard, or include unrelated
changes. Limit review to the change paths if they separate cleanly.
Otherwise stop and ask.

Find the base after `git fetch origin`:

- PR: `gh pr view <n> --json baseRefName,headRefOid`. Check out the branch
  only if clean. Confirm `HEAD` is the PR head, or ahead only by this
  change. Base: `git merge-base HEAD origin/<baseRefName>`.
- Local: `git merge-base HEAD origin/<default-branch>`. No remote: a base
  the user names, or `HEAD` for uncommitted changes only.

The change is base to working tree in those paths, with untracked files.
Use one diff command all rounds. State intent and out-of-scope in 1-2
sentences. Run covering checks. Do not send code this change breaks. Note
missing or pre-failing checks in the brief.

## 2. Start Sol

In T3, call `orchestrator_capabilities`. Pick the latest Sol unless the user
named a version. Do not hardcode an ID. Record provider, model, and effort
only if exposed. Use `delegate_task` every round (`role: "review"`,
`mode: "async"`). Save `taskId`. New `clientRequestId` per round.
`childThreadId` is storage, not the next target. Do not use
`t3_thread_send`, `create_threads`, or `t3_thread_launch` for review.

If T3 tools are not listed, try one direct capability call. Outside T3, use
a native Sol subagent and keep its ID. In Claude Code, use a custom subagent
only if it is set up to run Sol. If no route runs Sol, report the blocker. Do
not substitute a model.

Do not edit scoped files while review runs. Wait for the notice. Do not
poll or start a second reviewer. Timeout, error, or no reply is not
approval. On failure, cancel, verify stop, restart with the ledger.

Round 1 brief (T3 children get no history):

```
Review only. Do not edit, commit, push, comment on PRs, or start subagents.
Repo: <abs path> Base: <sha> Intent: <intent> Out of scope: <scope> Checks: <results>
See: git diff <base> [-- <paths>]; git status --short (read untracked).
Read surrounding code. Find bugs, broken callers, mismatch with intent.
Skip style unless it hides a bug. Hold to the smallest change. Flag code,
tests, or guards the intent does not need. Other paths, rare cases, small
perf, extra compat: nits.
blocker = intended case wrong. should = real bug callers will hit, in intent. nit = rest.
Reply:
VERDICT: APPROVE or CHANGES
S1 [blocker|should|nit] <file>:<line> <claim>. Fix: <suggestion> (stable ids)
```

## 3. Answer findings

Check each finding and severity yourself. Another path, rare case, or
small cost is a nit, whatever label it came with.

- Agree: smallest fix. Prefer delete or narrow over new lock, cache,
  helper, or option. Fix the case that happened. Add one focused test
  that fails without the fix, if intent needs it.
- Disagree: say why, with evidence (file:line, test, output).
- Out of scope or nit: decline in one line. List as follow-up.

Update the ledger. Re-run checks and `git diff --shortstat <base>`. If
review grew the diff, cut first. Do not agree just to end the loop.

## 4. Next round

Start one only if budget remains and a blocker or should is open, behavior code
changed, or approval does not cover the current behavior diff. Use a fresh
`delegate_task` in T3, or follow up the saved native ID. Send the round 1 brief,
the ledger (`fixed:` / `disagree:` / `declined:` + evidence), the same base
diff, and the change since last round. Tell Sol: open ids and changed code only.
Mark each old id `resolved` or `still open: <reason>`.

## 5. Stop and ship

Agreed: APPROVE on the current behavior diff, no blocker or should open,
no concern of your own. Stuck: an item stays disputed after two replies,
or budget ends. Show both sides in 2-3 lines each. The user decides.
Budget end is not approval.

Do not push during the loop. Push after agreement only if the user asked
to push, ship, or update the PR. If you push to a PR, add above the model
blurb:

`Reviewed with sol-loop: <N> rounds with <model>. Sol verdict: approved`.

Add `on <effort>` only if verified.

Report: rounds, model, what Sol changed, diff size before/after, fixed and
declined findings with reasons, usage if exposed (else say not), pushed or not.

## T3 Code orchestration

Ordinary coding tasks need no T3 tools.

- Subagents: use your native tool when the child uses your provider, a model it offers, and no settings beyond yours, and it finishes in this turn (Claude `Agent` always with `run_in_background:false`; Codex `spawn_agent`, then wait). Use `delegate_task` for another provider's model, user-asked settings, a separate checkout (`isolation:"worktree"`), background work, or `delegate_task` by name. A native type running another provider's model counts too. Workflow only when asked.
- Call `orchestrator_capabilities` once per thread, before the first `delegate_task`. Again only after an error or a user-named provider change. Settings go in `target.options`. Provider or model unavailable: say so. Never switch unasked, or fall back to native tools, Workflow, or CLIs. Never make a child's checkout in the shell or in `task`.
- Every new delegate review or re-check is a new `delegate_task` (brief, findings, objections), never a `t3_thread_send`. Fix small review findings yourself; start no delegate for them. When told to proceed without a delegate, or to run fewer, `task_cancel` the extras. Start no replacement.
- Follow a running delegate's `next`. Do not poll it (`task_status`, `sleep`, watchers, Monitor, ScheduleWakeup). Stop a delegate run you replace or no longer need with `task_cancel`, never `t3_thread_interrupt` on a `childThreadId`.
- If you are a subagent or child, do the work yourself. Start no subagents unless your task says to.

- `t3_thread_launch` and `create_threads` make new top-level threads, only when the user asks for a new thread. "Subagent", "delegate", and "parallel" never mean one. Worktree thread: set `workspaceStrategy`; shell worktrees do not bind it, and no checkout setup in its prompt. No `workspaceStrategy`: project root, not your worktree.
- Given a thread id, `t3_thread_read` it before you answer about it.
- In your reply, a thread's first mention is its `link` verbatim. No `link`: `[title](t3-thread://v1/<exact id>)`. Never a plain title or bare id.
- A secret: call `request_secret` yourself. Pass its `secretRef` to a T3 tool, or use `delivery: "file"` for a shell command. Never ask in chat or invent one. When asked only to schedule, `schedule_task` without running its prompt.
- T3 tools may load late. Try the name once before you call it absent.

### Visuals and preview

- Answer data with a trend or comparison with a chart, and show any visual the user asks for here: pass its HTML to `html_preview`, then `html_render`. If the visual is a file, pass that file's HTML. A screenshot on disk or a text description does not show it. Never start a server for it. Tools a web page exposes give data only. Never use them to show results. Asked for an image to post, send, or use elsewhere: a `.png` file and its path, never `html_render`.
- Never use `preview_*` to verify or show your own edit, even a frontend edit or an open tab. Do not repeat preview calls from an earlier turn. Use them only when the current request asks for browser work or names a page or tab. Public pages: web fetch or search unless browser work was asked; then preview tools only, no web fetch. Close a tab you opened before you reply, unless the user asked for it or uses it.


### Background work you wait on

To wait for a background command or Monitor you started (tests, a build), call `t3_background_wait` with its task ID before you end your turn. Do not mark work you leave running, or PRs. T3 MCP tools are deferred: load one with ToolSearch before you call it.

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this agent. Set this ONLY when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask that this agent or delegated work run at a specific effort level, never on your own judgment; otherwise omit it and the agent runs at its usual effort. Ignored for subagent_type: "fork": a fork runs at your own effort.

run_in_background.description: Agents run in the background by default; you will be notified when one completes. Set to false only when your very next action depends on this agent's result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise leave it in the background so the user can hand you other work.

isolation.description: Isolation mode. "worktree" creates a temporary git worktree so the agent works on an isolated copy of the repo. "remote" launches the agent in a remote cloud environment (always runs in background; availability is gated).

tools.name: AskUserQuestion
tools.description:
Use this tool only when you are blocked on a decision that is genuinely the user's to make: one you cannot resolve from the request, the code, or sensible defaults.

Usage notes:
- Users will always be able to select "Other" to provide custom text input
- Use multiSelect: true to allow multiple answers to be selected for a question
- If you recommend a specific option, make that the first option in the list and add "(Recommended)" at the end of the label

Plan mode note: To switch into plan mode, use EnterPlanMode (not this tool). Once in plan mode, use this tool to clarify requirements or choose between approaches BEFORE finalizing your plan. Do NOT use this tool to ask "Is my plan ready?", "Should I proceed?", or otherwise reference "the plan" in questions — the user cannot see the plan until you call ExitPlanMode for approval.

Reserve this for decisions where the user's answer changes what you do next — not for choices with a conventional default or facts you can verify in the codebase yourself. In those cases pick the obvious option, mention it in your response, and proceed.

The user may see only the question dialog: tool results and text you wrote earlier in this turn may not be on their screen while it is open. Make each question stand on its own: if it depends on something you found, say so briefly, and name the items you are asking about in the question itself.

questions.description: Questions to ask the user (1-4 questions)

question.description: The complete question to ask the user. Should be clear, specific, and end with a question mark. Example: "Which library should we use for date formatting?" If multiSelect is true, phrase it accordingly, e.g. "Which features do you want to enable?"

header.description: Very short label displayed as a chip/tag (max 12 chars). Examples: "Auth method", "Library", "Approach".

options.description: The available choices for this question. Must have 2-4 options. Each option should be a distinct, mutually exclusive choice (unless multiSelect is enabled). There should be no 'Other' option, that will be provided automatically.

label.description: The display text for this option that the user will see and select. Should be concise (1-5 words) and clearly describe the choice.

description.description: Explanation of what this option means or what will happen if chosen. Useful for providing context about trade-offs or implications.

preview.description: Optional preview content rendered when this option is focused. Use for mockups, code snippets, or visual comparisons that help users compare options. See the tool description for the expected content format.

multiSelect.description: Set to true to allow the user to select multiple options instead of just one. Use when choices are not mutually exclusive.

answers.description: User answers collected by the permission component

annotations.description: Optional per-question annotations from the user (e.g., notes on preview selections). Keyed by question text.

preview.description: The preview content of the selected option, if the question used previews.

notes.description: Free-text notes the user added to their selection.

metadata.description: Optional metadata for tracking and analytics purposes. Not displayed to user.

source.description: Optional identifier for the source of this question (e.g., "remember" for /remember command). Used for analytics tracking.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 1800000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background. With it, `timeout` limits how long the command may run in the background before it is stopped (default 1800000 ms, max 7200000 ms).

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to modify

new_string.description: The text to replace it with (must be different from old_string)

replace_all.description: Replace all occurrences of old_string (default false)

tools.name: ListAgents
tools.description: Lists agents you can SendMessage to — in-process subagents you spawned, the teammates on your team, other local Claude sessions on this machine, your Claude sessions running in the cloud (when this session has cloud access; a cloud session receives your message but cannot message any session back yet — do not ask it to reply, read its answer in its own transcript), and (when Remote Control is connected here) your account's other sessions — Remote Control sessions on other machines and cloud sessions, each row labeled by kind. Names are the address: send with `SendMessage({to: "<name>", message: "..."})`, copying the name exactly as a row prints it. Append a row's ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — two rows share it, or an error asks you to disambiguate.

channel.description: Not available in this build; leave unset.

q.description: Not available in this build; leave unset.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.name: ReportFindings
tools.description: Report code-review findings as a typed list so the host UI can render them. Use this only when the active code-review instructions tell you to report findings with this tool; otherwise follow whatever output format those instructions specify. When reporting a review's results, call it once with the verified findings ranked most-severe first (empty array if nothing survived verification) and do not also print the findings as text. When re-reporting after applying fixes (only if the apply instructions ask for it), set `outcome` on each finding to what actually happened.

level.description: Effort level the review ran at

findings.description: Verified findings, most-severe first; empty if none survived

file.description: Repo-relative path of the file the finding is in

short_summary.description: Compressed label for compact UI (≤60 chars): the claim alone, no rationale or consequence clause

category.description: Short kebab-case slug of the finding type, e.g. "correctness", "simplification", "efficiency", "test-coverage"

verdict.description: Set when a verify pass ran; absent on inline-only reviews

outcome.description: Set ONLY when re-reporting after applying fixes: what happened to this finding

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

args.description: Optional arguments for the skill

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

tools.name: Write
tools.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem, overwriting if one exists.

When to use: creating a new file, or fully replacing one you've already Read. Overwriting an existing file you haven't Read will fail. For partial changes, use Edit instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to write (must be absolute, not relative)

content.description: The content to write to the file

tools.name: mcp__linear-server__get_issue
tools.description: Retrieve detailed information about an issue by ID, including attachments, git branch name, and active Triage Intelligence suggestions when the issue is in triage. A nonempty fields selection overrides the include options; request optional fields directly in fields.

id.description: Issue ID or identifier (e.g., LIN-123). P-prefixed identifiers (e.g., P-ENG-123) are projects, not issues

fields.description: Fields to include in each result. Explicitly requested fields with no value return null. `id` is always included. Omit or pass an empty array for the default response.

tools.name: mcp__linear-server__list_comments
tools.description: List comments on a Linear issue, project, initiative, document, project milestone, or project/initiative status update. Provide exactly one of `issueId`, `projectId`, `initiativeId`, `documentId`, `milestoneId`, or `statusUpdateId`. `statusUpdateType` applies only to `statusUpdateId`; omit it for every other parent. For issues, projects, and initiatives this returns both top-level discussion threads and inline description comments. Inline (anchored) comments carry a non-null `quotedText` set to the snippet of description text they reference. Returned comments include `author` and nullable `onBehalfOf`; when set, `onBehalfOf` identifies the user the agent author acted for. Files uploaded in comment bodies are returned in `attachments` with titles and download URLs, not issue attachment IDs. Signed upload URLs expire after five minutes; call list_comments again to refresh them. Download documents using these URLs and process them with your own file tools.

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return per page

cursor.description: Omit for the first page. To continue, pass the previous response's cursor when hasNextPage is true

orderBy.description: Timestamp to sort results by: creation time or last update time

issueId.description: Issue ID or identifier (e.g., LIN-123). P-prefixed identifiers (e.g., P-ENG-123) are projects, not issues (provide exactly one parent)

projectId.description: Project name, ID, identifier (e.g., P-ENG-123), or slug (provide exactly one parent)

initiativeId.description: Initiative name, ID, identifier (e.g., I-123), or slug (provide exactly one parent)

documentId.description: Document ID or slug (provide exactly one parent)

milestoneId.description: Milestone UUID (provide exactly one parent). Resolve milestone names via `list_milestones` first.

statusUpdateId.description: Status update UUID (provide exactly one parent). Resolve status updates via `get_status_updates` first.

statusUpdateType.description: Set only together with `statusUpdateId`; omit for issue, project, initiative, document, and milestone comments. Type of status update named by `statusUpdateId`, as returned by `get_status_updates`. Omit to check both project and initiative status updates.

tools.name: mcp__linear-server__save_comment
tools.description: Create or update a comment on a Linear issue, project, initiative, document, project milestone, or project/initiative status update. If `id` is provided, updates the existing comment; otherwise creates a new one. To start a new thread, pass `body` and exactly one of `issueId`, `projectId`, `initiativeId`, `documentId`, `milestoneId`, or `statusUpdateId` (`statusUpdateType` applies only to `statusUpdateId`; omit it for every other parent) — comments on issues/projects/initiatives become top-level discussion threads; comments on documents/milestones become description comments. A status update holds a single thread, so a comment on an update that already has one is added to it as a reply. To reply to an existing thread, pass `parentId` and `body`; the reply inherits the parent's thread type, so no entity reference is needed. Parent reference fields are ignored when `id` or `parentId` is provided (`statusUpdateType` is rejected instead).

id.description: Comment ID. If provided, updates the existing comment

issueId.description: Issue ID or identifier (e.g., LIN-123). P-prefixed identifiers (e.g., P-ENG-123) are projects, not issues (provide exactly one parent)

projectId.description: Project name, ID, identifier (e.g., P-ENG-123), or slug (provide exactly one parent)

initiativeId.description: Initiative name, ID, identifier (e.g., I-123), or slug (provide exactly one parent)

documentId.description: Document ID or slug (provide exactly one parent)

milestoneId.description: Milestone UUID (provide exactly one parent). Resolve milestone names via `list_milestones` first.

statusUpdateId.description: Status update UUID (provide exactly one parent). Resolve status updates via `get_status_updates` first.

statusUpdateType.description: Set only together with `statusUpdateId`; omit for issue, project, initiative, document, and milestone comments. Type of status update named by `statusUpdateId`, as returned by `get_status_updates`. Omit to check both project and initiative status updates.

parentId.description: Parent comment ID (for replies, only when creating)

body.description: Content as Markdown. Do not escape the string — use literal newlines and special characters, not escape sequences. To mention a user, use @displayName (e.g., @johndoe). To embed an image or file, upload it with prepare_file_upload and insert the returned markdown

Intent (WEV-4197, product decision recorded on WEV-4196): GrowthOS (Accenture) users should get Persona Chat (the Pulse "Assistant") by default.
- wevo-pulse: GrowthOS's `pulse.findings_completed` webhook sends `pulseLink`, which GrowthOS stores once. `_share_url` in backend/app/services/growthos_pulse_webhooks.py now (a) creates the completion share row with share_assistant_chat=True and chat_shared_by_subject_id=owner when the Pulse has an owner (the public chat conversation is owned by chat_shared_by_subject_id; see app/services/public_pulse_chat_service.py), and (b) drops the hardcoded hideAssistant=true from the link so the share row's own chat setting decides (customer-app SharedFindingsPage shows chat only when the public assistant endpoint says enabled AND the URL lacks hideAssistant=true). Existing share rows are reused unchanged.
- customer-app: in src/components/pulse/components/PulseHeader.tsx, under the GrowthOS theme (theme.name === 'purple'), opening "Send to Discover" for a wevo-pulse-backed report turns share chat on (PATCH via updateShareAssistantChat) if it is off, and the "Include Assistant chat" toggle is hidden. Outside GrowthOS the toggle and behavior are unchanged.
Out of scope: customer-api-backed reports (still force hideAssistant=true); links already sent to GrowthOS with hideAssistant=true; data backfill of existing share rows.
Checks run: wevo-pulse `make finish-work` (targeted gate: format, lint, mypy, tests, complexity) passed; 201 GrowthOS backend tests pass and the 2 updated assertions fail on the old code. customer-app `yarn code-quality` (lint+typecheck+format) passed; PulseHeader.rootRoute.test.tsx 51 pass, the new GrowthOS test fails on the old code. Real-browser harness capture confirmed GrowthOS modal PATCHes {shareAssistantChat:true}, shows no toggle, URL has hideAssistant=false; classic theme unchanged.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this agent. Set this ONLY when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask that this agent or delegated work run at a specific effort level, never on your own judgment; otherwise omit it and the agent runs at its usual effort. Ignored for subagent_type: "fork": a fork runs at your own effort.

Set to false only when your very next action depends on this agent's result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise leave it in the background so the user can hand you other work.
