- Use multiSelect: true to allow multiple answers to be selected for a question

Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

args.description: Optional arguments for the skill

tools.name: TaskStop
tools.description:
- Stops a running background task by its ID
- Takes a task_id parameter identifying the task to stop
- To stop an agent-team teammate, pass its agent ID or bare teammate name as task_id
- To stop a background agent spawned with a name, pass that name as task_id
- Returns a success or failure status
- Use this tool when you need to terminate a long-running task

task_id.description: The ID of the background task to stop. Agent-team teammates and named background agents are also accepted by agent ID or name.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

# Babysit PR

Many repos have AI review bots. They're helpful, even if they are not always
right.

## Waiting

Never write your own watcher, polling loop, or `sleep` loop. Use one watcher
per PR: `watch_pull_request` in T3 Code, `pr-wait` everywhere else. Never run
both on the same PR. Every watcher on a GitHub account shares one rate limit.

### In T3 Code: `watch_pull_request`

Handle the existing checks and comments first. Then call
`watch_pull_request` and end your turn. T3 Code wakes you with a message when
a check fails, the required checks pass, someone comments or reviews, or the
branch conflicts.

- **Only the thread that owns the PR watches it.** If you are a delegated
  child task (a reviewer, a Sol round, any `delegate_task` child), never call
  `watch_pull_request`. The parent owns the PR. Do not watch PRs you are not
  working on.
- **A wake is news, not a merge decision.** Check the merge gate yourself.
- **Unwatch when you hand off.** A watched thread stays in Working and out of
  the user's inbox. When you stop (ready, blocked, or asking the user a question),
  call `unwatch_pull_request` first. A merge or close ends the watch on its
  own.
- **"Stopped watching, could not read it"** usually means GitHub's rate limit
  is used up. Run `gh api rate_limit --jq .resources.graphql` before you
  watch again. If `remaining` is near 0, wait for `reset` with one background
  command, then watch again. Never watch again in a tight loop.

### Everywhere else: `pr-wait`

Wait with `scripts/pr-wait` from this skill's directory (use its absolute
path).

```bash
pr-wait <pr> [--repo owner/name] [--until ready|green|any-change]
```

It prints one line per real event. It exits 0 when the `--until` condition is
met or the PR merges, 1 when it needs you (a required check failed, conflicts,
unresolved threads, PR closed), and 2 on bad input.

- `ready` (default): required checks green, Greptile or Macroscope reviewed the
  head, and no unresolved threads. Use this to babysit.
- `green`: required checks only. Use it when the repo has no Greptile or
  Macroscope.
- `any-change`: exit on the first event.

In Claude Code, run it with the Monitor tool (`timeout_ms: 3600000`), so each
line wakes you. Without a monitor, run it as one long command. It ends on its
own.

Start it again after you push, after you handle an exit 1, and after a resume.
It remembers what it already reported, so nothing that arrived in between is
lost. If it says another pid already watches the PR, do not start a second one.
Kill the old one only if its events do not reach you.

With either watcher: when an event needs no action, end your turn without a
message. Never post or say "still waiting".

## GitHub rate limits

`gh pr create`, `gh pr view`, and `gh pr checks` use GraphQL. When GraphQL is
used up, the REST limit is separate and usually still has room. Use
`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls/<n>` to read a PR, and
`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/commits/<sha>/check-runs` for checks.

## Reviews

Only act on checks and comments newer than the latest push. Verify every bot
finding against the source before changing code. Fix real findings and CI
failures, distinguish repository failures from infrastructure flakes, and reply
with a written reason when dismissing false positives.

If the repo has `.macroscope/check-run-agents/*.md`, read those rules before you
reply to a Macroscope finding. Its findings cite them.

CodeRabbit is advisory. Treat its findings like any other finding, but never
wait for it and never hold a merge for it.

If a review bot leaves feedback you believe is not worth addressing, reply with
a written reason and resolve the comment. Use the `leaving-pr-comments` skill
for every comment posted on the user's behalf.

Screenshots and videos help as well, when you have a way to upload them.

Keep the PR at the size the user's goal needs. Review loops tend to grow a
PR one cheap-looking fix at a time. Fix real bugs in the intended case.
Decline the rest with a written reason, and list them as follow-ups:
unneeded tests, guards for edge cases that do not matter, extra integration
or compatibility, and small performance costs. Prefer the fix that deletes or
narrows code.

## Base branch and merging

Keep an eye on changes to `main` and rebase when needed. `pr-wait` reports when
new base commits touch this PR's files, and when the PR becomes BEHIND or DIRTY.
`watch_pull_request` reports conflicts only, so check for BEHIND yourself
before you call the PR ready.
If an overlapping PR makes this one obsolete, stop monitoring, report it to the
user, and ask before closing the PR unless closure was explicitly authorized.

If nothing has changed, stay quiet rather than posting filler comments. Stop
when `pr-wait` exits 0, or in T3 Code when the merge gate passes on the latest
head. Merge only when the user explicitly requested it;
otherwise report that the PR is ready. Right before a merge, run `git fetch` and
check the PR again. Never merge when it is BEHIND or DIRTY, or when base commits
that landed after the last green run touch this PR's files. Rebase, push, and
wait for green again.

description.description: Explanation of what this option means or what will happen if chosen. Useful for providing context about trade-offs or implications.

preview.description: Optional preview content rendered when this option is focused. Use for mockups, code snippets, or visual comparisons that help users compare options. See the tool description for the expected content format.

multiSelect.description: Set to true to allow the user to select multiple options instead of just one. Use when choices are not mutually exclusive.

answers.description: User answers collected by the permission component

annotations.description: Optional per-question annotations from the user (e.g., notes on preview selections). Keyed by question text.

preview.description: The preview content of the selected option, if the question used previews.

notes.description: Free-text notes the user added to their selection.

metadata.description: Optional metadata for tracking and analytics purposes. Not displayed to user.

source.description: Optional identifier for the source of this question (e.g., "remember" for /remember command). Used for analytics tracking.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 1800000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background. With it, `timeout` limits how long the command may run in the background before it is stopped (default 1800000 ms, max 7200000 ms).

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to modify

new_string.description: The text to replace it with (must be different from old_string)

replace_all.description: Replace all occurrences of old_string (default false)

tools.name: ListAgents
tools.description: Lists agents you can SendMessage to — in-process subagents you spawned, the teammates on your team, other local Claude sessions on this machine, your Claude sessions running in the cloud (when this session has cloud access; a cloud session receives your message but cannot message any session back yet — do not ask it to reply, read its answer in its own transcript), and (when Remote Control is connected here) your account's other sessions — Remote Control sessions on other machines and cloud sessions, each row labeled by kind. Names are the address: send with `SendMessage({to: "<name>", message: "..."})`, copying the name exactly as a row prints it. Append a row's ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — two rows share it, or an error asks you to disambiguate.

channel.description: Not available in this build; leave unset.

q.description: Not available in this build; leave unset.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.name: ReportFindings
tools.description: Report code-review findings as a typed list so the host UI can render them. Use this only when the active code-review instructions tell you to report findings with this tool; otherwise follow whatever output format those instructions specify. When reporting a review's results, call it once with the verified findings ranked most-severe first (empty array if nothing survived verification) and do not also print the findings as text. When re-reporting after applying fixes (only if the apply instructions ask for it), set `outcome` on each finding to what actually happened.

level.description: Effort level the review ran at

findings.description: Verified findings, most-severe first; empty if none survived

file.description: Repo-relative path of the file the finding is in

short_summary.description: Compressed label for compact UI (≤60 chars): the claim alone, no rationale or consequence clause

category.description: Short kebab-case slug of the finding type, e.g. "correctness", "simplification", "efficiency", "test-coverage"

verdict.description: Set when a verify pass ran; absent on inline-only reviews

outcome.description: Set ONLY when re-reporting after applying fixes: what happened to this finding

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

args.description: Optional arguments for the skill

tools.name: TaskStop
tools.description:
- Stops a running background task by its ID
- Takes a task_id parameter identifying the task to stop
- To stop an agent-team teammate, pass its agent ID or bare teammate name as task_id
- To stop a background agent spawned with a name, pass that name as task_id
- Returns a success or failure status
- Use this tool when you need to terminate a long-running task

task_id.description: The ID of the background task to stop. Agent-team teammates and named background agents are also accepted by agent ID or name.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

tools.name: Write
tools.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem, overwriting if one exists.

When to use: creating a new file, or fully replacing one you've already Read. Overwriting an existing file you haven't Read will fail. For partial changes, use Edit instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to write (must be absolute, not relative)

content.description: The content to write to the file

tools.name: mcp__linear-server__get_issue
tools.description: Retrieve detailed information about an issue by ID, including attachments, git branch name, and active Triage Intelligence suggestions when the issue is in triage. A nonempty fields selection overrides the include options; request optional fields directly in fields.

id.description: Issue ID or identifier (e.g., LIN-123). P-prefixed identifiers (e.g., P-ENG-123) are projects, not issues

fields.description: Fields to include in each result. Explicitly requested fields with no value return null. `id` is always included. Omit or pass an empty array for the default response.

tools.name: mcp__linear-server__list_comments
tools.description: List comments on a Linear issue, project, initiative, document, project milestone, or project/initiative status update. Provide exactly one of `issueId`, `projectId`, `initiativeId`, `documentId`, `milestoneId`, or `statusUpdateId`. `statusUpdateType` applies only to `statusUpdateId`; omit it for every other parent. For issues, projects, and initiatives this returns both top-level discussion threads and inline description comments. Inline (anchored) comments carry a non-null `quotedText` set to the snippet of description text they reference. Returned comments include `author` and nullable `onBehalfOf`; when set, `onBehalfOf` identifies the user the agent author acted for. Files uploaded in comment bodies are returned in `attachments` with titles and download URLs, not issue attachment IDs. Signed upload URLs expire after five minutes; call list_comments again to refresh them. Download documents using these URLs and process them with your own file tools.

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return per page

cursor.description: Omit for the first page. To continue, pass the previous response's cursor when hasNextPage is true

orderBy.description: Timestamp to sort results by: creation time or last update time

issueId.description: Issue ID or identifier (e.g., LIN-123). P-prefixed identifiers (e.g., P-ENG-123) are projects, not issues (provide exactly one parent)

projectId.description: Project name, ID, identifier (e.g., P-ENG-123), or slug (provide exactly one parent)

initiativeId.description: Initiative name, ID, identifier (e.g., I-123), or slug (provide exactly one parent)

documentId.description: Document ID or slug (provide exactly one parent)

milestoneId.description: Milestone UUID (provide exactly one parent). Resolve milestone names via `list_milestones` first.

statusUpdateId.description: Status update UUID (provide exactly one parent). Resolve status updates via `get_status_updates` first.

statusUpdateType.description: Set only together with `statusUpdateId`; omit for issue, project, initiative, document, and milestone comments. Type of status update named by `statusUpdateId`, as returned by `get_status_updates`. Omit to check both project and initiative status updates.

tools.name: mcp__linear-server__save_comment
tools.description: Create or update a comment on a Linear issue, project, initiative, document, project milestone, or project/initiative status update. If `id` is provided, updates the existing comment; otherwise creates a new one. To start a new thread, pass `body` and exactly one of `issueId`, `projectId`, `initiativeId`, `documentId`, `milestoneId`, or `statusUpdateId` (`statusUpdateType` applies only to `statusUpdateId`; omit it for every other parent) — comments on issues/projects/initiatives become top-level discussion threads; comments on documents/milestones become description comments. A status update holds a single thread, so a comment on an update that already has one is added to it as a reply. To reply to an existing thread, pass `parentId` and `body`; the reply inherits the parent's thread type, so no entity reference is needed. Parent reference fields are ignored when `id` or `parentId` is provided (`statusUpdateType` is rejected instead).

id.description: Comment ID. If provided, updates the existing comment

issueId.description: Issue ID or identifier (e.g., LIN-123). P-prefixed identifiers (e.g., P-ENG-123) are projects, not issues (provide exactly one parent)

projectId.description: Project name, ID, identifier (e.g., P-ENG-123), or slug (provide exactly one parent)

initiativeId.description: Initiative name, ID, identifier (e.g., I-123), or slug (provide exactly one parent)

documentId.description: Document ID or slug (provide exactly one parent)

milestoneId.description: Milestone UUID (provide exactly one parent). Resolve milestone names via `list_milestones` first.

statusUpdateId.description: Status update UUID (provide exactly one parent). Resolve status updates via `get_status_updates` first.

statusUpdateType.description: Set only together with `statusUpdateId`; omit for issue, project, initiative, document, and milestone comments. Type of status update named by `statusUpdateId`, as returned by `get_status_updates`. Omit to check both project and initiative status updates.

parentId.description: Parent comment ID (for replies, only when creating)

body.description: Content as Markdown. Do not escape the string — use literal newlines and special characters, not escape sequences. To mention a user, use @displayName (e.g., @johndoe). To embed an image or file, upload it with prepare_file_upload and insert the returned markdown

tools.name: mcp__linear-server__save_issue
tools.description: Create or update a Linear issue. If `id` is provided, updates the existing issue; otherwise creates a new one. When creating, `team` is required, and `title` is required unless `template` is set. Note: use `assignee` (not `assigneeId`) to set the assignee — it accepts a user ID, name, email, or "me".

id.description: Only for updating an existing issue. Pass the issue ID or identifier (e.g., LIN-123). Do NOT pass this parameter when creating a new issue.

title.description: Issue title (required when creating, unless template is set)

description.description: Content as Markdown. Do not escape the string — use literal newlines and special characters, not escape sequences. To mention a user, use @displayName (e.g., @johndoe)

patch.description: Partial edits applied to the current content, in order and atomically (one failing operation aborts the whole save). Every anchor string must match the current content exactly once. Only valid on update, in place of the full content/description field

old_string.description: Exact text to replace. Must match the current content exactly once

new_string.description: Replacement text. Empty string deletes the match

replace_all.description: Replace every occurrence instead of requiring a unique match

anchor.description: Exact text to insert before. Must match the current content exactly once

text.description: Text to insert directly before the anchor. Include separators (e.g. "\n\n")

anchor.description: Exact text to insert after. Must match the current content exactly once

text.description: Text to insert directly after the anchor. Include separators (e.g. "\n\n")
Text to insert at the very start of the content
Text to insert at the very end of the content

from.description: Exact text where the range starts (inclusive). Must match exactly once

to.description: Exact text where the range ends (exclusive, stays in place). Must match exactly once after `from`

new_string.description: Text replacing the range. Empty string deletes it

team.description: Team name or ID (required when creating)

cycle.description: Cycle name, number, or ID. Null to remove

project.description: Project name, ID, identifier (e.g., P-ENG-123), or slug. Null to remove

assignee.description: User ID, name, email, or "me". Null to remove

delegate.description: Agent name or ID. When the user asks to delegate to "Linear" or "the Linear agent", this refers to the "Linear" app user specifically. Null to remove

labels.description: Label names or IDs as a JSON array of strings (e.g. ["Bug", "Urgent"]). Replaces the full label set; existing labels not included are removed. Omit to leave labels unchanged. Cannot be combined with addLabels/removeLabels; prefer those for incremental changes

addLabels.description: Label names or IDs as a JSON array of strings (e.g. ["Bug", "Urgent"]) to add. Append-only; existing labels are never removed. Cannot be combined with a team change

removeLabels.description: Label names or IDs as a JSON array of strings (e.g. ["Bug", "Urgent"]) to remove. Only valid when updating an existing issue. Cannot be combined with a team change

dueDate.description: Due date (ISO format). On update, pass null to remove the due date

slaBreachesAt.description: ISO-8601 timestamp when the SLA will breach. On update, pass null to remove the SLA

slaType.description: SLA day counting type: "all" or "onlyBusinessDays". Only use with slaBreachesAt; null means unset

parentId.description: Parent issue ID or identifier (e.g., LIN-123). Null to remove

estimate.description: Issue estimate value. On create, pass null or omit for no estimate. On update, pass null to clear the estimate; omitting leaves it unchanged. 0 is a real estimate only on teams that allow zero estimates.

links.description: Link attachments to add [{url, title}]. Append-only; existing links are never removed

setReleases.description: Replace all releases on the issue with these. Cannot be combined with addReleases/removeReleases

blocks.description: Issue IDs/identifiers this blocks. Append-only; existing relations are never removed

tools.name: mcp__t3-code__delegate_task
tools.description: Start one child agent with only `task`. No parent history. Separate checkout or PR per child: `isolation:'worktree'`. Keep `taskId` for `task_status` and `task_cancel`.

options.description: Options from `orchestrator_capabilities`, such as {effort:'max'}. Given values override inherited. [] or {} clears.

isolation.description: 'shared' (default): parent checkout. 'worktree': new prepared checkout from the parent commit, for a separate checkout or PR per child. Uncommitted edits stay out.

mode.description: Default 'async'. 'wait' only if this turn needs the result. A question or approval ends the wait.

timeoutMs.description: Mode 'wait' only. Default 10 min. A timeout does not cancel the child.

runtimeMode.description: Omit unless the user asks for a supervised child. Narrow modes pause for human approval, not read-only. Above yours is rejected.

tools.name: mcp__t3-code__orchestrator_capabilities

tools.name: mcp__t3-code__task_cancel

entries.description: Create or update a Linear issue. If `id` is provided, updates the existing issue; otherwise creates a new one. When creating, `team` is required, and `title` is required unless `template` is set. Note: use `assignee` (not `assigneeId`) to set the assignee — it accepts a user ID, name, email, or "me".

id.description: Only for updating an existing issue. Pass the issue ID or identifier (e.g., LIN-123). Do NOT pass this parameter when creating a new issue.

title.description: Issue title (required when creating, unless template is set)

description.description: Content as Markdown. Do not escape the string — use literal newlines and special characters, not escape sequences. To mention a user, use @displayName (e.g., @johndoe)

patch.description: Partial edits applied to the current content, in order and atomically (one failing operation aborts the whole save). Every anchor string must match the current content exactly once. Only valid on update, in place of the full content/description field

old_string.description: Exact text to replace. Must match the current content exactly once

new_string.description: Replacement text. Empty string deletes the match

replace_all.description: Replace every occurrence instead of requiring a unique match

anchor.description: Exact text to insert before. Must match the current content exactly once

text.description: Text to insert directly before the anchor. Include separators (e.g. "\n\n")

anchor.description: Exact text to insert after. Must match the current content exactly once

text.description: Text to insert directly after the anchor. Include separators (e.g. "\n\n")
Text to insert at the very start of the content
Text to insert at the very end of the content

from.description: Exact text where the range starts (inclusive). Must match exactly once

to.description: Exact text where the range ends (exclusive, stays in place). Must match exactly once after `from`

new_string.description: Text replacing the range. Empty string deletes it

team.description: Team name or ID (required when creating)

template.description: Template name or ID. Applied on create only. The template fills in the content, fields, and sub-issues server-side. A `description` replaces the template body rather than merging with it, but an empty `description` keeps the template body. Labels merge with the template's own

cycle.description: Cycle name, number, or ID. Null to remove

project.description: Project name, ID, identifier (e.g., P-ENG-123), or slug. Null to remove

assignee.description: User ID, name, email, or "me". Null to remove

delegate.description: Agent name or ID. When the user asks to delegate to "Linear" or "the Linear agent", this refers to the "Linear" app user specifically. Null to remove

labels.description: Label names or IDs as a JSON array of strings (e.g. ["Bug", "Urgent"]). Replaces the full label set; existing labels not included are removed. Omit to leave labels unchanged. Cannot be combined with addLabels/removeLabels; prefer those for incremental changes

addLabels.description: Label names or IDs as a JSON array of strings (e.g. ["Bug", "Urgent"]) to add. Append-only; existing labels are never removed. Cannot be combined with a team change

removeLabels.description: Label names or IDs as a JSON array of strings (e.g. ["Bug", "Urgent"]) to remove. Only valid when updating an existing issue. Cannot be combined with a team change

dueDate.description: Due date (ISO format). On update, pass null to remove the due date

slaBreachesAt.description: ISO-8601 timestamp when the SLA will breach. On update, pass null to remove the SLA

slaType.description: SLA day counting type: "all" or "onlyBusinessDays". Only use with slaBreachesAt; null means unset

parentId.description: Parent issue ID or identifier (e.g., LIN-123). Null to remove

estimate.description: Issue estimate value. On create, pass null or omit for no estimate. On update, pass null to clear the estimate; omitting leaves it unchanged. 0 is a real estimate only on teams that allow zero estimates.

links.description: Link attachments to add [{url, title}]. Append-only; existing links are never removed

setReleases.description: Replace all releases on the issue with these. Cannot be combined with addReleases/removeReleases

addReleases.description: Release IDs or slugs to add. Append-only; existing releases are never removed

removeReleases.description: Release IDs or slugs to remove. Only valid when updating an existing issue

blocks.description: Issue IDs/identifiers this blocks. Append-only; existing relations are never removed

blockedBy.description: Issue IDs/identifiers blocking this. Append-only; existing relations are never removed

relatedTo.description: Related issue IDs/identifiers. Append-only; existing relations are never removed

duplicateOf.description: Duplicate of issue ID/identifier. Null to remove

**Merged (Claude, 10-29)**

PRs
- wevo-pulse #955 (https://github.com/wevo-conversion/wevo-pulse/pull/955), squash `772c3e72`, on main
- customer-app #2985 (https://github.com/wevo-conversion/customer-app/pull/2985), squash `cb5c07a7`, on staging

Root cause: GrowthOS stores `pulseLink` once at completion. `_share_url` hardcoded `hideAssistant=true`, and since #952 completion also creates the share with `share_assistant_chat=false`. Every new GrowthOS link would hide Persona Chat for good.

Fix
- wevo-pulse: the share that completion creates turns on the owner's Assistant chat (`chat_shared_by_subject_id` = owner, who also owns the public conversation). `pulseLink` drops `hideAssistant`, so the share row's own setting decides and a later toggle reaches links already stored. Existing shares are reused unchanged. Pulses with no owner keep chat off. `docs/growthos-integration.md` updated.
- customer-app: under the GrowthOS theme, opening Send to Discover on a WEVO Pulse report PATCHes `shareAssistantChat: true` if it's off, and hides the toggle. The URL stays in "Loading share URL…" until that resolves, so a `hideAssistant=true` link can't be copied mid-request. Classic theme unchanged.

Proof
- Backend: updated assertions fail on the old code and pass with the fix. 173 GrowthOS tests green after rebase, `make finish-work` clean, CI green.
- Frontend: new `PulseHeader.rootRoute.test.tsx` case fails without the change, including the pending-PATCH copy guard. `yarn code-quality` and CI green.
- Real browser (visual-baseline harness, mocked APIs): GrowthOS dialog sent PATCH `{shareAssistantChat:true}`, rendered no toggle, URL ended `hideAssistant=false`. Classic dialog still showed the toggle, sent no PATCH, and kept `hideAssistant=true`.
- Reviewed with sol-loop: 2 rounds, gpt-6.1-sol, approved (one finding fixed: the copy-before-PATCH race).

Deploy state
- Not in Stage or prod yet. **Do not deploy wevo-pulse tag 0.1.233 to prod by itself**: it has #952 without this fix, so every new GrowthOS link would hide chat. Cut the next release from main (contains both #952 and `772c3e72`). customer-app needs a release from staging containing `cb5c07a7`.

Open items
- Verified in production: not done. Prod kube API was unreachable from here (VPN down).
- Links already stored in GrowthOS with `hideAssistant=true` (e.g. Jessica's Oct 27-28 Pulses) still hide chat. Restoring them needs a GrowthOS-side link update or a customer-app override; out of scope here.
- customer-api-backed reports still force `hideAssistant=true` (out of scope per ticket).

Still open on this ticket
- Prod check of Jessica's 3 Pulses (project 66d63523-5d34-41a1-b992-aebc2b446417): not done. The prod kube API timed out from here (VPN down). The queries in the first comment are still the ones to run.
- Links GrowthOS already stored for her Oct 27-28 Pulses carry `hideAssistant=true`, so the fix won't bring chat back on those. New Pulses after deploy get chat.
- Reply to Kerry, and an answer on Jessica's credit request: not done (customer-facing, needs a human).

{"id":"WEV-4196","uuid":"d7af68fa-208e-45de-a573-cc8b98e5aa6a","title":"Persona Chat missing on GrowthOS Pulse links (Accenture)","description":"**Problem**
Jessica Garrido (Accenture, GrowthOS project 66d63523-5d34-41a1-b992-aebc2b446417) reports Persona Chat no longer appears on her recent completed Pulses and is asking for credits back for the 3 Pulses where it was missing. Accenture (Kerry McElhaney) expects chat to be available to GrowthOS users after findings generate, says it was for months, and is asking why it was turned off and for it to be turned back on. Support told Kerry on Oct 29 that chat is "not enabled by default within GrowthOS" and this is expected behavior; Kerry has disputed that in writing to Henry, Nitzan and Andrea, so the customer is waiting on a corrected answer.

Decision needed: should chat be available on the Pulse link GrowthOS stores? Options: (a) keep it hidden on share links, as today per <issue id="14dc6fb9-7e30-4afb-bf78-04a8e1f61372" href="https://linear.app/wevo/issue/WEV-3510/limit-share-url-when-pulse-is-created-from-growthos-generic">WEV-3510</issue>; (b) honor the per-Pulse "Include Assistant chat" toggle on that link; (c) default chat on for GrowthOS-created Pulses.

**What Accenture has told us (from Kerry's Oct 29 email)**

* Jul 29: WEVO Engineering told them this was intended behavior: chat available on the [WEVO.ai](<http://WEVO.ai>) site after findings, not through the GrowthOS share URL. Accenture read that as "chat is available after findings."
* Week of Sep 9: Jordan Kerzee and Nitzan met and, per Kerry, concluded chat should be turned on for GrowthOS users after findings generate. That decision is not recorded in Linear.
* Oct 5: GrowthOS users started seeing the Discover link with an "Include Assistant Chat" toggle on the Send to Discover modal and read that as chat being supported for them.
* Oct 28: Jessica reports chat gone from the top right on her last 3 Pulses, with a before/after screenshot. Her Accenture workspace usage: 1 Pulse on Oct 12, 1 on Oct 26, 3 on Oct 27, 1 on Oct 28.
* Oct 29, 9:04 AM: Support (Lucía S.) replied that chat is not enabled by default within GrowthOS and this is expected.
* Oct 29, 9:22 AM: Kerry disputed that reply and asked (1) why it was disabled now and (2) to have it turned back on. No decision to discontinue was communicated to GrowthOS.

Email thread (Nitzan and Henry forwards): [https://mail.google.com/mail/u/0/#inbox/FMfcgzQjggkVcmRHZczbfNfdWKgbWTDw](<https://mail.google.com/mail/u/0/#inbox/FMfcgzQjggkVcmRHZczbfNfdWKgbWTDw>)

**Done when**

- [X] Product decision recorded on this ticket, including what Nitzan and Jordan actually agreed in September
- [ ] Prod check confirms which link and backend Jessica's 3 Pulses use and what changed between her Oct 12 Pulse (chat present) and Oct 27-28 Pulses (chat missing)
- [X] If enabling: chat shows on the GrowthOS link after findings, with a regression test
- [ ] Verified in production
- [ ] Reply sent to Kerry correcting the Oct 29 support response, with the decision and timing
- [ ] Credit request for Jessica's 3 Pulses answered

**Pointers**

* wevo-pulse `growthos_pulse_webhooks.py:121` (`_share_url`, prod 0.1.231) hardcodes `hideAssistant=true` since #196 (Aug 11)
* `models/pulse_share_link.py:133`: `share_assistant_chat` defaults false
* Inference: wevo-pulse #952 (<issue id="c6b3c25b-7d3b-4fc6-bcb3-359903a6b496" href="https://linear.app/wevo/issue/WEV-4154/completed-growthos-pulse-shows-pulse-unavailable-for-project-members">WEV-4154</issue>, Oct 28, not yet in prod) creates a share row at every completion, which would hide chat on every new GrowthOS link for owners too
* Slack: [https://wevo-internal.slack.com/archives/C73QBFG3D/p1793280816388399](<https://wevo-internal.slack.com/archives/C73QBFG3D/p1793280816388399>)
* Related: <issue id="14dc6fb9-7e30-4afb-bf78-04a8e1f61372" href="https://linear.app/wevo/issue/WEV-3510/limit-share-url-when-pulse-is-created-from-growthos-generic">WEV-3510</issue>, <issue id="c6b3c25b-7d3b-4fc6-bcb3-359903a6b496" href="https://linear.app/wevo/issue/WEV-4154/completed-growthos-pulse-shows-pulse-unavailable-for-project-members">WEV-4154</issue>, <issue id="33d53d99-8650-430d-8a3a-773dac09eb7c" href="https://linear.app/wevo/issue/WEV-4087/completed-growthos-pulses-missing-from-pulse-history-accenture">WEV-4087</issue>, <issue id="f40b5c05-e76a-4417-a589-b99b3d29aa7e" href="https://linear.app/wevo/issue/WEV-4043/download-and-send-to-discover-buttons-missing-on-growthos-pulse">WEV-4043</issue>","priority":{"value":3,"name":"Medium"},"url":"https://linear.app/wevo/issue/WEV-4196/persona-chat-missing-on-growthos-pulse-links-accenture","gitBranchName":"ryan/wev-4196-persona-chat-missing-on-growthos-pulse-links-accenture","createdAt":"2026-10-29T13:47:08.179Z","updatedAt":"2026-10-29T14:51:45.110Z","archivedAt":null,"completedAt":null,"startedAt":null,"canceledAt":null,"dueDate":null,"slaStartedAt":null,"slaMediumRiskAt":null,"slaHighRiskAt":null,"slaBreachesAt":null,"status":"Triage","statusType":"triage","labels":["Agent: created","Customer Support","Enhancement","Product Decision"],"attachments":[{"id":"1567bb0f-391a-4ab9-9964-dad39462d8df","title":"Email: Kerry McElhaney dispute, Oct 29","subtitle":null,"url":"https://mail.google.com/mail/u/0/#inbox/FMfcgzQjggkVcmRHZczbfNfdWKgbWTDw"}],"documents":[],"createdBy":"Customer Support","createdById":"a31621c8-ef38-4d66-aaf4-abebca0f2b99","project":"GrowthOS Integration (Accenture)","projectId":"3928c3fe-7f7d-44ee-8f8f-9c8e23c39b65","team":"WEVO","teamId":"4a449dea-46d3-4339-ad7a-089eb32b9f22"}

input.body:
**Merged (Claude, 10-29)**

PRs
- wevo-pulse #955 (https://github.com/wevo-conversion/wevo-pulse/pull/955), squash `772c3e72`, on main
- customer-app #2985 (https://github.com/wevo-conversion/customer-app/pull/2985), squash `cb5c07a7`, on staging

Root cause: GrowthOS stores `pulseLink` once at completion. `_share_url` hardcoded `hideAssistant=true`, and since #952 completion also creates the share with `share_assistant_chat=false`. Every new GrowthOS link would hide Persona Chat for good.

Fix
- wevo-pulse: the share that completion creates turns on the owner's Assistant chat (`chat_shared_by_subject_id` = owner, who also owns the public conversation). `pulseLink` drops `hideAssistant`, so the share row's own setting decides and a later toggle reaches links already stored. Existing shares are reused unchanged. Pulses with no owner keep chat off. `docs/growthos-integration.md` updated.
- customer-app: under the GrowthOS theme, opening Send to Discover on a WEVO Pulse report PATCHes `shareAssistantChat: true` if it's off, and hides the toggle. The URL stays in "Loading share URL…" until that resolves, so a `hideAssistant=true` link can't be copied mid-request. Classic theme unchanged.

Proof
- Backend: updated assertions fail on the old code and pass with the fix. 173 GrowthOS tests green after rebase, `make finish-work` clean, CI green.
- Frontend: new `PulseHeader.rootRoute.test.tsx` case fails without the change, including the pending-PATCH copy guard. `yarn code-quality` and CI green.
- Real browser (visual-baseline harness, mocked APIs): GrowthOS dialog sent PATCH `{shareAssistantChat:true}`, rendered no toggle, URL ended `hideAssistant=false`. Classic dialog still showed the toggle, sent no PATCH, and kept `hideAssistant=true`.
- Reviewed with sol-loop: 2 rounds, gpt-6.1-sol, approved (one finding fixed: the copy-before-PATCH race).

Deploy state
- Not in Stage or prod yet. **Do not deploy wevo-pulse tag 0.1.233 to prod by itself**: it has #952 without this fix, so every new GrowthOS link would hide chat. Cut the next release from main (contains both #952 and `772c3e72`). customer-app needs a release from staging containing `cb5c07a7`.

Open items
- Verified in production: not done. Prod kube API was unreachable from here (VPN down).
- Links already stored in GrowthOS with `hideAssistant=true` (e.g. Jessica's Oct 27-28 Pulses) still hide chat. Restoring them needs a GrowthOS-side link update or a customer-app override; out of scope here.
- customer-api-backed reports still force `hideAssistant=true` (out of scope per ticket).

**Fix merged via WEV-4197 (Claude, 10-29)**

Implements the decision (GrowthOS users get Persona Chat by default): wevo-pulse #955 (`772c3e72`) and customer-app #2985 (`cb5c07a7`). Details, proof, and deploy notes are on WEV-4197. Neither is deployed yet. Don't ship wevo-pulse 0.1.233 alone: it has #952 without this fix.

Still open on this ticket
- Prod check of Jessica's 3 Pulses (project 66d63523-5d34-41a1-b992-aebc2b446417): not done. The prod kube API timed out from here (VPN down). The queries in the first comment are still the ones to run.
- Links GrowthOS already stored for her Oct 27-28 Pulses carry `hideAssistant=true`, so the fix won't bring chat back on those. New Pulses after deploy get chat.
- Reply to Kerry, and an answer on Jessica's credit request: not done (customer-facing, needs a human).

Once #952 ships, every GrowthOS completion gets a share link with chat sharing off and `hideAssistant=true`, so GrowthOS users lose Persona Chat (Accenture report, WEV-4196). Ryan's decision (10-29): GrowthOS users get the agent by default, including in Send to Discover; the chat enable/disable toggle applies only to non-GrowthOS Discover URL generation.

**Done when**

- [X] Share links created for GrowthOS completions default to chat enabled
- [X] The `pulseLink` sent to GrowthOS no longer hardcodes `hideAssistant=true`

Fix

- customer-app: under the GrowthOS theme, opening Send to Discover on a WEVO Pulse report PATCHes `shareAssistantChat: true` if it's off, and hides the toggle. The URL stays in "Loading share URL…" until that resolves, so a `hideAssistant=true` link can't be copied mid-request. Classic theme unchanged.

- Reviewed with sol-loop: 2 rounds, gpt-6.1-sol, approved (one finding fixed: the copy-before-PATCH race).

description: Exact merge-to-Stage sequence per repo (wevo-pulse main → Dev CI proof → release → credit audit → scheduler activation; customer-app and wevo-artemis staging → release-and-deploy-stage) with the gotchas hit on 2026-10-17

- **customer-app**: squash-merge into `staging`, then immediately `gh workflow run release-and-deploy-stage.yml -R wevo-conversion/customer-app --ref staging -f auto_version=patch`. The run builds the frontend itself (~15 min incl. quality jobs). Merged PRs on 2026-10-17 used squash (merge commits have one parent).
- **wevo-artemis**: squash-merge into `staging`. `ci.yml` only runs on PRs; the dev image `artemis:dev-<short7>` is built by `deploy-duplo.yml` on the push to staging (~3 min). `release-and-deploy-stage.yml` (ref staging, patch) retags that dev image, so wait for the push build to finish first or the retag step fails.
- **wevo-pulse**: squash-merge into `main`. Stage needs `release-and-deploy-stage.yml` dispatched from main with `operation=release candidate_sha=<full main sha> auto_version=patch`; `verify_candidate` requires that exact SHA's `code-quality.yml` push run to have succeeded *including* the Dev deploy jobs (dev image proof). Push runs on main are serialized by concurrency group; a pending push run can be cancelled when another lands, so always confirm the candidate's own run is `success` before dispatching. The release pauses the Stage Celery scheduler; afterwards run `apply-stage-pulse-runtime-config.yml` (`operation=audit`, `release_run_id=<release run>`), then `activate-stage-celery-scheduler.yml` (`cutoff` ISO-8601 with tz at least 24h old, `credit_audit_run_id`, `release_run_id`, `confirmation=RECONCILE STALE STAGE TASKS`). Prior successful sequence: release 38986173670 → audit 38989142173 → activation 38989652162 (Pulse 0.1.213, cutoff 2026-10-16T00:04:12+00:00, 0 stale tasks).
- **wevo-pulse gotchas learned 2026-10-17 (0.1.214/0.1.215)**: (a) the release workflow's final job "MANDATORY: Audit Credits, Then Activate Scheduler" only writes a handoff summary; it runs nothing, so the Stage scheduler stays paused until the audit and activation workflows are dispatched by hand. (b) The audit's `verify-release-candidate` (scripts/stage_release_proof.py `_latest_release`) takes the newest `workflow_dispatch` run of release-and-deploy-stage.yml by created_at and requires it to be the reviewed run with conclusion success. A duplicate dispatch that gets cancelled (even with 0 jobs) becomes the newest run and makes every audit fail with "Latest Stage release is not the reviewed successful SHA". Recovery is to re-release the same candidate SHA (new patch tag) so a successful run is newest, then audit against that new run id; do not dispatch the release workflow again until the audit has run. Never double-dispatch: check `gh run list --workflow release-and-deploy-stage.yml` before dispatching. (c) `reconcile_stale_tasks` rejects an apply cutoff newer than 24 h; a cutoff ~25 h old worked. Sequence for 0.1.215: release 39058230003 → audit 39060572799 (10 deployments, 0 reconciliation) → activation 39060896806.
- **artemis / customer-app on 2026-10-17 17:17 UTC**: artemis #1177 → 0.1.37 (release run 39053341330, dispatched from the GitHub UI 3 min after merge once the dev image build finished); customer-app #2961 → 0.1.271 (run 39053068046). When several agent sessions share the user's gh token, use ListAgents/SendMessage to agree on one release operator before dispatching anything.
- `gh` is not on the Bash tool PATH; use `export PATH="/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/local/bin:$PATH"`. zsh does not word-split unquoted vars, so `set -- $spec` loops need `${=spec}` or a function.

**How to apply:** follow this order when asked to "get work into staging"; see [[wevo-stage-readonly-data-access]] and [[wevo-prod-access-and-topology]] for access and prod promotion.
- **2026-10-17 0.1.216-era release (PR #911, candidate ebd0314d)**: release 39074124634 → audit 39076527158 failed with "Reading live credit-tracking state for personas-api failed" (a `kubectl exec printenv` with 20 s timeout right after rollout; transient) → re-dispatched audit 39076704253 succeeded (safe because the newest release run was still the reviewed success) → activation 39076931422 (cutoff now-25h). Coordinate with the 44-case suite session via SendMessage before dispatch so it holds new journey launches.
- When the Duplo JIT credential (`duplo-creds.json` Expiration) has lapsed, `duploctl jit ... --interactive` exits 147 "Failed to get token" without a TTY; only the user can re-login, so plan Stage verification that doesn't need kube (GitHub workflows, browser timings).

- **2026-10-18 (0.1.217/0.1.218)**: activation 39101780720 for release 39099402811 failed at its last step "Validate and enrich Stage task recovery canary evidence" with "Canary worker pod is not in the exact-digest fleet proof" (worker pod changed between fleet proof and canary); the workflow re-paused the scheduler itself (step 24). Recovery was a fresh release of the newer main SHA (b4900d73) → audit → activation, which succeeded. `finish-work` (make finish-work / scripts/run_finish_work.py) is the only way to write a patch changeset; a failed run keeps a pending receipt that produces a duplicate changeset on the next run (delete one), and repeated `--scope` keeps only the last value (edit the YAML).

Recovery that worked: release the next green main SHA, then audit and activation again. Two sessions shared Stage; agree via SendMessage who dispatches, and one holds.
- Release, audit and activation each take about 30-60 min; the release often exceeds a 30-min Monitor window, so re-arm the watch.
- **2026-10-18 0.1.219 (candidate 8ee8bf45, #914+#915)**: release 39168034193 → audit 39171609849 → activation 39171868509 (cutoff now-25h), all first-try green. customer-app 0.1.27x releases 39154814477 (#2963), 39164666073 (#2962), 39173738928 (#2964).
